# `nish/net/quic-conn-params`

QUIC's transport parameters (RFC 9000 §18), the bytes each endpoint carries in TLS's `quic_transport_parameters` extension (RFC 9001 §8.2), encoded and parsed.

```ts
import {
  QUIC_MIN_UDP_PAYLOAD,
  QUIC_TP_ACK_DELAY_EXPONENT,
  QUIC_TP_ACTIVE_CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT,
  QUIC_TP_DISABLE_ACTIVE_MIGRATION,
  QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_DATA,
  QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAMS_BIDI,
  QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAMS_UNI,
  QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAM_DATA_BIDI_LOCAL,
  QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAM_DATA_BIDI_REMOTE,
  QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAM_DATA_UNI,
  QUIC_TP_INITIAL_SCID,
  QUIC_TP_MAX_ACK_DELAY,
  QUIC_TP_MAX_DATAGRAM_FRAME_SIZE,
  QUIC_TP_MAX_IDLE_TIMEOUT,
  QUIC_TP_MAX_UDP_PAYLOAD_SIZE,
  QUIC_TP_ORIGINAL_DCID,
  QUIC_TP_PREFERRED_ADDRESS,
  QUIC_TP_RETRY_SCID,
  QUIC_TP_STATELESS_RESET_TOKEN,
  QuicTransportParameters,
  quicEncodeTransportParameters,
  quicEncodeTransportParametersInto,
  quicParseTransportParameters,
  quicParseTransportParametersInto,
} from "nish/net/quic-conn-params";
```

```ts
import { QuicTransportParameters, quicEncodeTransportParameters,
         quicParseTransportParameters } from "nish/net/quic-conn-params";

const mine: QuicTransportParameters = new QuicTransportParameters()
mine.initialMaxData = 65536
const bytes: u8[] = quicEncodeTransportParameters(mine)   // for TlsServerConfig
// bytes is [0x04, 0x04, 0x80, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00]: initial_max_data, length 4, 65536
const theirs: QuicTransportParameters = quicParseTransportParameters(bytes, false)
if (theirs.error !== 0) {
  // close the connection with theirs.error; theirs.errorParameter names the parameter
}
```

The transport parameters `p` as the `quic_transport_parameters` extension's body (§18): each parameter as its ID, its length and its value, in ID order, every varint-valued one only when it is not its default, every byte-valued one only when its `has*` flag is set, and `disable_active_migration` only when true.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-detail title="Defaults">

A `QuicTransportParameters` starts at every parameter's
default (§18.2), so a parse leaves a parameter the peer did not send at the value the RFC
says it then has. The encoder writes a parameter only when it differs from
that default, plus the connection IDs, which have none.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**What a parse refuses.** Each of these is a TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR
(§7.4, §18.2): an ID or a length that does not fit, a parameter running past the bytes, a
known parameter sent twice, a varint-valued parameter whose value is not
exactly one varint, `disable_active_migration` with a value, a server-only
parameter from a client (`original_destination_connection_id`,
`preferred_address`, `retry_source_connection_id`,
`stateless_reset_token`), a stateless reset token that is not 16 bytes, a
connection ID over 20 bytes, `max_udp_payload_size` below 1200,
`ack_delay_exponent` above 20, `max_ack_delay` at 2^14 or above,
`active_connection_id_limit` below 2, and a stream count above 2^60.
Unknown parameters, the reserved ones (31 × N + 27) among them, are
skipped, as §18.1 asks; a second copy of an unknown one is not noticed.
Whether `initial_source_connection_id` is present and right is the
connection's check, because it needs the packet the ID came in.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Provenance">

Written from RFC 9000 §18, in this module's own structure; nothing here is
ported from another implementation. Private names carry the
`quicParams` prefix (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e).

</scalar-detail>

## quicEncodeTransportParameters

The transport parameters `p` as the `quic_transport_parameters`
extension's body (§18): each parameter as its ID, its length and its
value, in ID order, every varint-valued one only when it is not its
default, every byte-valued one only when its `has*` flag is set, and
`disable_active_migration` only when true. Nothing is checked: these are
this endpoint's own values, and a value no varint holds is left out.

```ts
function quicEncodeTransportParameters(
  p: QuicTransportParameters,
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="p" type="QuicTransportParameters" required>

This endpoint's parameters, only read.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

A new array holding the extension body; empty when every parameter is at its default.

</scalar-field>

## quicEncodeTransportParametersInto

`quicEncodeTransportParameters` into `out`, which is emptied first: the
encoding is pushed into the room the array already has, so a connection
slot that keeps one array for its parameters grows it only when they
outgrow every earlier connection's.

```ts
function quicEncodeTransportParametersInto(
  p: QuicTransportParameters,
  out: u8[],
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="p" type="QuicTransportParameters" required>

This endpoint's parameters, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array the extension body replaces the contents of.

</scalar-field>

## quicParseTransportParameters

Parses the body of a `quic_transport_parameters` extension. `fromServer`
says who sent it, which decides whether the server-only parameters are
allowed. The answer's `error` is `QUIC_ERROR_NO_ERROR`, or
`QUIC_ERROR_TRANSPORT_PARAMETER` for any of the breaks the module header
lists, with `errorParameter` naming the parameter; on an error the other
fields hold what was read so far and are not to be used.

```ts
function quicParseTransportParameters(
  bytes: u8[],
  fromServer: boolean,
): QuicTransportParameters
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="bytes" type="u8[]" required>

The extension body as the peer sent it, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="fromServer" type="boolean" required>

True when the peer is the server, so that the server-only parameters are allowed.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicTransportParameters">

A new `QuicTransportParameters`; read its `error` before any other field.

</scalar-field>

## quicParseTransportParametersInto

`quicParseTransportParameters` into `p`, which is set back to every
default first, its byte-valued fields emptied and refilled in the room
their arrays have: a connection slot parses each client's parameters into
one object of its own. Answers `p`.

```ts
function quicParseTransportParametersInto(
  p: QuicTransportParameters,
  bytes: u8[],
  fromServer: boolean,
): QuicTransportParameters
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="p" type="QuicTransportParameters" required>

The object to overwrite with the parsed parameters and the verdict in `error`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="bytes" type="u8[]" required>

The extension body as the peer sent it, only read.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="fromServer" type="boolean" required>

True when the peer is the server, so that the server-only parameters are allowed.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="QuicTransportParameters">

`p` itself; read its `error` before any other field.

</scalar-field>

## QuicTransportParameters

One endpoint's transport parameters. Every field starts at the default
§18.2 gives it, and the connection IDs and token start empty with their
`has*` flag false. `preferredAddress` is kept as the bytes the server sent,
since this side never acts on it. `error` is what a parse answers:
`QUIC_ERROR_NO_ERROR`, or `QUIC_ERROR_TRANSPORT_PARAMETER` with
`errorParameter` the ID of the parameter at fault (-1 when the bytes did not
frame).

```ts
class QuicTransportParameters
```

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="1,200" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_MIN_UDP_PAYLOAD: i64`

The smallest `max_udp_payload_size` allowed, and every QUIC path's minimum datagram (RFC 9000 §14).

</scalar-card>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="0x0a" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_ACK_DELAY_EXPONENT: i32`

`ack_delay_exponent`: an ACK Delay field counts units of 2^this microseconds; at most 20, default 3.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0e" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_ACTIVE_CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT: i32`

`active_connection_id_limit`: how many of the peer's connection IDs the sender keeps; at least 2, the
default.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0c" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_DISABLE_ACTIVE_MIGRATION: i32`

`disable_active_migration`: present, with no value, when the sender takes no connection migration.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x04" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_DATA: i32`

`initial_max_data`: the connection-wide flow-control limit, in bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x08" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAMS_BIDI: i32`

`initial_max_streams_bidi`: how many bidirectional streams the peer may open; at most 2^60.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x09" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAMS_UNI: i32`

`initial_max_streams_uni`: how many unidirectional streams the peer may open; at most 2^60.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x05" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAM_DATA_BIDI_LOCAL: i32`

`initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local`: the flow-control limit, in bytes, for bidirectional streams the
sender opens.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x06" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAM_DATA_BIDI_REMOTE: i32`

`initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote`: the flow-control limit, in bytes, for bidirectional streams the peer
opens.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x07" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_INITIAL_MAX_STREAM_DATA_UNI: i32`

`initial_max_stream_data_uni`: the flow-control limit, in bytes, for unidirectional streams the peer opens.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0f" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_INITIAL_SCID: i32`

`initial_source_connection_id`: the Source Connection ID of the sender's first Initial.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0b" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_MAX_ACK_DELAY: i32`

`max_ack_delay`: the longest the sender delays an acknowledgement, in milliseconds; below 2^14, default 25.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x20" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_MAX_DATAGRAM_FRAME_SIZE: i32`

`max_datagram_frame_size` (RFC 9221 §3): the largest DATAGRAM frame, type
and Length included, the sender takes; absent or 0, it takes none.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x01" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_MAX_IDLE_TIMEOUT: i32`

`max_idle_timeout`, in milliseconds; 0 or absent for no idle timeout.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x03" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_MAX_UDP_PAYLOAD_SIZE: i32`

`max_udp_payload_size`: the largest UDP payload, in bytes, the sender takes; at least 1200, default 65527.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x00" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_ORIGINAL_DCID: i32`

`original_destination_connection_id`: the Destination Connection ID of the client's first Initial; server
only.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0d" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_PREFERRED_ADDRESS: i32`

`preferred_address`: an address the server would have the client move to; server only.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_RETRY_SCID: i32`

`retry_source_connection_id`: the Source Connection ID of the server's Retry, when it sent one; server
only.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x02" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_TP_STATELESS_RESET_TOKEN: i32`

`stateless_reset_token`: the 16-byte token for the server's first connection ID; server only.

</scalar-card>
